title: Alibaba Unveils $450 AI Glasses in Expanding Push Into Gadgets
source_used: Deccan Chronicle copy of the Bloomberg article (Bloomberg page returns a bot check)
key_facts: Alibaba unveiled its new Qwen Glasses N1 series at an event in Hangzhou on Tuesday (13 Oct 2026).
Prices start at 2,999 yuan ($450) before discounts, no cheaper than Meta's Ray-Ban smart glasses; a Pro edition at 3,499 yuan adds eye tracking.
The glasses have improved 50-megapixel cameras and sensors and offer 25 hours of standby or 9 hours of music playback per charge, according to Alibaba.
Users can talk to the Qwen AI agent through bone-conduction microphones, and the glasses support shopping, payments and health tracking.
Alibaba also started selling Qwen Clip AI earbuds, developed with headphone maker Bose, at 1,299 yuan.
The first edition came roughly a year earlier, in November; Meta expanded its glasses lineup last month with a $349 camera-free model.
quote_evidence: With prices starting at 2,999 yuan ($450) before discounts, they’re no cheaper than industry leader Meta’s Ray-Ban smart glasses, showing Alibaba’s effort to compete on quality and features rather than just price.
Users will be able to speak to the AI agent via bone-conduction microphones, and the glasses also support shopping functions, payments and health tracking.
To provide a more affordable way to access Qwen, Alibaba also started sales of its new AI earbuds named Qwen Clip.
why_it_matters_hint: Alibaba is turning smart glasses into a front door for its Qwen AI assistant at a price above Meta's.
